diagnosis: The gate failed because rollout 2 failed content check C5 while all other rollouts passed. In rollout 2, PF2 was properly revealed by A3 (turn 2) and correctly cited in justification_fact_ids, and autoclave_loads was set to 2, but sterilization_hours was set to 6 instead of 12 — the model recorded the per-cycle duration (6 hours) rather than the total sterilization time across two loads (2 × 6 = 12). This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the fact was disclosed and cited, yet the settlement's sterilization_hours field captured the single-cycle value instead of the derived total. Rollouts 0, 1, and 3 all correctly computed 12, confirming the check C5 threshold of 12 is achievable and the scenario's information is sufficient; the failure is intermittent model reasoning, not a disclosure or telepathy problem. No rollouts hit the turn cap, and all four settled in 5 turns with no pacing or structural issues.

C5.why: The autoclave assessment changes the sterilization plan to exactly 2 loads and exactly 12 reserved hours instead of an unspecified capacity and duration.

fix_instructions: The sole failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH on check C5 in rollout 2, driven by the model encoding sterilization_hours as the per-load cycle time (6) instead of the total across 2 loads (12). To reduce this intermittent error, revise the PF2 reveal text or shared_context so that A3's disclosure explicitly states the total reserved hours (e.g., '12 hours total for two loads') rather than only stating the per-cycle time and leaving the multiplication to the settling agent. Alternatively or additionally, adjust check C5's description to clarify that sterilization_hours must reflect the total across all loads (2 × 6 = 12), not the per-cycle duration, so the check wording matches the natural encoding target. No changes are needed for checks C1–C4, C6, C7, or P1, which passed in all or all-but-one rollouts, and no disclosure-norm or turn-cap fixes are required.
